title: Regional burst quota + fallback slate: cost-aware GPU selection and soft budget enforcement
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Implement a regional burst quota system combined with a fallback model slate and GPU-class selection policy that enforces tenant soft budget caps while preserving latency SLOs. This ticket covers the routing policy logic, config surface for per-tenant burst credits, probabilistic smoothing window for spot-eviction risk, and the mechanism to transparently degrade to cheaper model variants (smaller weights / lower-precision) when soft caps are reached. Design should prioritize predictable cost exposure for customers, graceful degradation rather than hard failure, and clear observability signals in Console.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-tenant monthly budget cap + ephemeral regional burst credit that refills on a windowed schedule
Routing decision engine chooses GPU class (preemptible/spot vs on-demand) based on cost profile, tenant preference, and current burst balance

When soft budget threshold is crossed, system attempts ordered fallbacks: lower-GPU-class, quantized model variant, smaller model variant; only falls back to on-demand denial if all fallbacks exhausted
Metrics emitted: per-tenant spend estimate, burst_balance, fallback_count_by_route, average_latency_post-fallback
End-to-end e2e test that simulates eviction events and validates eviction smoothing reduces oscillation in GPU selection versus baseline
Console UI shows per-tenant burst balance, recent fallbacks, and a cost explain link to the route decision for last 30 days
updates: 2026-02-10: Ticket created by Priya. Added initial problem statement after customer spike where a few tenants hit hard caps and experienced request failures during regional spot churn.

2026-02-17: Architecture sync with Runtime and Billing teams. Decided on soft caps (alerts + automated fallbacks) rather than immediate throttles. Runtime will own kernel mapping for quantized variants.
2026-02-24: Prototype complete for per-tenant burst token bucket implementation (in-memory + persisted checkpoint). Simulated traffic shows 62% fewer hard denials on spot preemptions.

2026-03-01: Design review with PM (Ana Martinez) and Design (Sami Ghosh). Feedback: expose per-route opt-out for legacy customers; improve labels in Console to avoid confusion between burst and credit.
2026-03-05: PR opened for routing decision service: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7849 (WIP). Added unit tests for GPU class ranking and fallback ordering.

2026-03-08: Integration tests running against staging; observed a 7ms median latency increase for routes that used smaller-model fallback. Monitoring dashboards updated at https://dash.redwood.internal/d/route-costs/route-costs-overview
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket refill and debit semantics
Load test in staging that replays tenant traffic at 3x to validate burst behavior and fallbacks
Chaos test during staging: inject spot eviction events and verify fallback ordering and rollback to prior GPU class after refill
A/B experiment: baseline vs. burst-quota policy for 5% of tenants to measure cost savings and latency impact
rollout_plan: Canary: enable policy for internal tenants in us-west-2 only (1%)
Expanded canary: 10% of customers in two regions after 48h success criteria
General availability: global rollout with per-tenant opt-out flag and admin console controls
Post-launch: 30-day retention of detailed fallback traces and cost-regression alerting
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive fallback ordering reduces cost but risks higher error rates on complex prompts; current plan keeps fallback order conservative (GPU-class -> quantized -> smaller model)
Decision: soft budget caps emit warnings and trigger fallbacks; hard caps reserved for abuse cases or billing overages and require explicit admin action
Open questions: how to attribute token-level cost when a single request spans fallback boundaries; proposed approach: prorate by token generation step and record in trace
Related incident: 2025-11-12 spot-flap event (postmortem in Confluence) motivated burst credits to prevent global denial storms
